document.abstract: In a communication addressed to the Chairman of the Committee by President Goldsmith, about the middle of March, the Committee was asked “…to formulate standards of sound recording and reproduction (audio-frequency characteristics) of such a type that the producing studios and the theater circuits can all agree to accept them at a reasonably early date after the standards shall have been agreed upon. The present state of sound recording and reproducing indicates that the matter is definitely urgent. There is an unnecessary amount of deviation in releases from the various studios, and it is obvious that the full advaniages of improved methods of reproduction can not be realized under the present conditions. Such standardization is the most important problem facing the Committee.”
